html:
SMTO-SKL-0067 — SMTO couldn't find that contact

GUID: 39445337-5fe6-50e6-89a3-c2387149a706
Slug: microsoft365-contact-not-found
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • The contact SMTO was asked to use isn't in this Microsoft 365 account. It may have been deleted or moved, or it's saved in a different account.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to search your contacts by name or email, for example "find my contact Maria Lopez". This gets the contact's current details, which change if it was deleted, merged or moved to another folder.
  2. Open Outlook People or Contacts and check whether the contact still exists; if you were deleting it, it may already be gone. If the contact is already gone, there is nothing left to do.
  3. If you have more than one Microsoft account, type @ and pick the account that holds this contact, then ask again. A contact saved in one account can't be found from another.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows or updates the contact you meant, and Outlook shows the same result.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to change a different contact with a similar name.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Microsoft Graph returned resource-not-found during a Microsoft 365 contact operation, so the contact or contact folder ID did not resolve for the selected account.

What this means

  • A resource-not-found response during a contact-prefixed operation is translated into the contact-not-found family. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • A resource-not-found response during a contact-prefixed operation is translated into the contact-not-found family.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact contact route and ID with the same account.

How to fix it

  • Search or list contacts again under the same account_ref and use the exact current contact_id and folder_id; do not substitute a contact from another account or tenant. If a delete was the original request, confirm whether the contact is already gone before issuing another change.
  • Read/search the same account again and use an exact current resource ID; do not substitute another account or tenant.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended accessible contact is resolved without account substitution.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
